turns.text: If we take Chinook apart, which idea truly changed the direction of research?

Checkers was complex enough to challenge contemporary search algorithms, yet structured enough for decades of endgame-database construction. That made Chinook an unusually productive bridge between competitive game programs and formal game solving.
That sounds like a promising direction. What mechanism actually makes it work?

Chinook combined opening knowledge, alpha-beta forward search, hand-built position evaluation, and solved endgame tables so current choices could connect to proven late-game outcomes. As the databases expanded, the unknown search space contracted until the team could establish a proof chain from the initial position to a draw.

Experts generally treat Chinook as a landmark in game-solving research and high-performance search. Its long-term legacy is showing how expert evaluation, alpha-beta search, opening knowledge, and endgame databases can combine to approach perfect play.
Seen alongside Temporal-Difference Update, Chinook reveals how the same technical question can echo across different eras.
